architectural_fidelity.reason: Room is clearly recognizable with same white walls, ceiling height, window position/size, wood flooring, and camera viewpoint maintained; LED strips retained as original feature

furniture_removal.reason: Original furniture NOT removed - gaming chair, keyboard/piano, and bed frame all remain visible; this is essentially the same room with blue lighting, not a redesign

style_commitment.reason: No mid-century modern style executed whatsoever - the room retains its original gaming/music aesthetic with blue LED lighting and sun tapestry; no MCM furniture, no period-appropriate palette

editorial_density.reason: Minimal staging - desk lamp, single decorative pillow, and wall art present but this appears to be the original room's existing items, not curated MCM styling with layered textiles or vignettes

photorealism.reason: Image is photorealistic with coherent lighting, proper shadows, and realistic material textures - no CGI artifacts or plastic feel

designer_preference_reason: Cova failed to perform the fundamental task of furniture removal and style transformation, delivering essentially the original room rather than a mid-century modern redesign.
what_cova_does_better: Preserves original LED strip lighting as an existing architectural feature
what_collov_does_better: Coherent style execution with appropriate furniture selections
Professional staging density with layered textiles and accessories
Clean slate transformation from original to target aesthetic
specific_fixes_if_failing: Remove ALL original furniture including gaming chair, keyboard, and bed frame completely
Replace with authentic mid-century modern pieces: low-profile platform bed with tapered legs, credenza or desk with MCM lines
Eliminate blue LED lighting or integrate subtly if keeping; add warm ambient lighting with arc floor lamp or period-appropriate fixtures
Remove gaming/music aesthetic entirely and commit to 1950s-60s palette: warm woods, earth tones, accent colors like mustard or teal
Add MCM-specific decor: geometric textiles, period art prints, sculptural elements, plants in ceramic planters
